newsitem.title: USA: Icahn sets terms for adviser in RJR move.
newsitem.headline: Icahn sets terms for adviser in RJR move.

text.p: Investor Carl Icahn disclosed in a regulatory filing Wednesday the terms a securities firm would get for its role over the next 12 months in the possible spinoff or splitup of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Icahn, RJR's largest individual shareholder, said Donaldson Lukfin & Jenrette would receive a $2.5 million retainer fee payable promptly upon execution of the pact.

Icahn's companies would also pay DLJ a monthly fee of $125,000 payable on the first business day of each month starting May 1, 1997 and from time to time reimburse all reasonable out-of-pocket expenses.

DLJ would get additional cash compensation at the end of 18 months based on the RJR's market price at that time, or earlier, in the event Icahn's companies -- High River, Meadow Walk, Barberry or American Real Estate Partners -- sold, diposed of or otherwise transfered within 18 months securities owned or acquired during the term of the agreement.
On January 27, High River, Meadow Walk and Barberry retained DLJ to act as their exclusive financial advisor for 12 months.
Icahn is launching a proxy fight aimed at forcing the company to spin off its 80.5 percent-owned Nabisco Holdings Corp subsidiary.
